title: Monoidal factorization of component inverse image
statement: Let T be an affine scheme and use the fixed component tests and inverse image of [def-zl-condensed-lisse-evaluation-model]. Assume test continuity, braidedness and preservation of finite limits and colimits. Restriction of abelian condensed sheaves to the profinite slice over pi_0(T), followed by component inverse image, is naturally isomorphic to the fixed point inverse image. The isomorphism is monoidal for the specified structures.

proof.text: Extract the chosen relative test functor and its natural projection and universal mapping property from component_relative_profinite_site. Continuity implies preservation of finite coproducts; finite limits identify the terminal test. Thus its composite with Over.star agrees with the absolute test functor on finite profinite spaces, by the finite coproduct comparison.

The relative universal mapping property gives preservation of the canonical finite-quotient limits after Over.star. The absolute test functor preserves these limits by profinite_test_object_functor. Extend the finite comparison using Profinite.functor_iso_of_finite, and cancel the fully faithful inclusion of the pro-etale site into schemes over the base.

Use the slice adjunction Over.forgetAdjStar on abelian sheaves and the sheafified Kan-extension adjunction of the fixed component inverse image. The natural test comparison identifies their composite right adjoint with the right adjoint of upperStarFromPoint. The adjunction conjugate is the required natural isomorphism.

On underlying presheaves, a natural transformation of continuous test functors induces monoidal restriction maps: the unit and tensor equations are naturality of the inclusion comparison maps. This makes the slice adjunction counit monoidal. The component pullback counit and point pullback unit are monoidal by the existing site tensor structures. Express the conjugate as the composite of these unit, restriction and counit maps, with functor associators and unitors. Every factor is monoidal, hence so is the comparison. Empty finite coproducts and all canonical finite-quotient limits are included.

Correct an arbitrary supplied braided structure by scalar multiplication with the ratio of its unit comparison and the canonical unit comparison. Naturality of unitors proves the unit equation; the unit-normalized tensor identity supplies the tensor equation. Whisker by slice restriction and compose with the canonical monoidal factorization.
